newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium, Fortis in talks about ASLK-CGER stake.
newsitem.headline: Belgium, Fortis in talks about ASLK-CGER stake.

text.p: Belgian-Dutch insurance and banking group Fortis and the Belgian government are in talks about the sale of a further stake in Belgian banking and insurance group ASLK/CGER to Fortis, both parties said on Thursday.

"The Belgian government is awaiting suggestions from the state privatisation committee about how the sale can be realised," Paul Van Rompuy, director of state-owned holding company FPM/SFP, which holds 49.9 percent of ASLK/CGER, said at ASLK/CGER's 1996 earnings news conference.
"We know that this year ASLK will be expected to make a contribution to the reduction of the Belgian state debt," Van Rompuy added.
Fortis acquired a 49.9 percent stake in ASLK in late 1993.
ASLK Bank and ASLK Insurance each hold 0.1 percent of the group's shares in autocontrol.

Under the terms of the 1993 privatisation, the Belgian state has a put option to sell another 9.8 percent stake in ASLK/CGER to Fortis and Fortis has a right of first refusal on a further 15 percent of ASLK.
The state's put option expires at the end of 1999.

Van Rompuy reiterated that a September 1993 Royal Decree stipulates that the reduction of the state's stake to 25.1 percent from 40.1 percent can only be done in three ways: a public sale, a bourse listing or a sale of shares to the bank's personnel.
Belgian Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt said earlier this year that he favours a bourse listing for ASLK/CGER.
Fortis managing director Valere Croes said on Thursday that the issue of a possible bourse listing for ASLK/CGER would be discussed by the Fortis board, but that no date had been set yet.

Fortis co-chairman Maurice Lippens said at Fortis's results news conference on Wednesday it was up to the state to decide if it wanted to go ahead with a bourse listing, but noted it could be risky for the reputation of the bank should the issue flop.
"I don't want to see our depositors getting their fingers burned and leaving us," he said.
ASLK/CGER chief executive Karel De Boeck said he could not comment on whether the bank itself was in favour of a listing or not. "We cannot comment as long as talks are being held," he said.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
